definitions.replacementCost: Primary seller-side build-versus-buy reference: estimated cost to recreate comparable present transferable work product.
definitions.marketComparableProxy: Marketability-weighted internal cost scenario. No observed comparable IP transaction is used.
definitions.incomeLicensingProxy: Monetization-weighted internal cost scenario. No project revenue, cash-flow forecast, DCF or royalty valuation is established.
definitions.probabilityAdjustedStrategicValue: Secondary buyer-side opportunity reference anchored to replacement cost and adjusted for technical completion, commercialization probability, rights-transfer reserve, time/risk and sector context.
definitions.triangulatedEconomicReference: Weighted internal cost-scenario blend. Shared inputs make the scenarios correlated; this is not independent triangulation or certified market value.
definitions.sellerAsk: Indicative seller-side source-code/IP acquisition asking reference positioned primarily against recreation cost.

methodology.lowestCostPolicy: Cost is distinct from market value. Existing seller asking references are separate transaction choices. New budgets use the lowest explicitly scoped low-effort scenario at EUR 94/hour plus 15%, rounded down to EUR 500. These estimates and retained legacy anchors do not establish an absolute cost floor, a market minimum, actual expenditure, attributable income or a completed sale.
assumptions: Engineering-equivalent effort is not recorded development time or actual expenditure.
The retained role budgets are analyst choices; Knab and Upwork provide context and do not endorse them.
The 15% coordination/tooling allowance is not added as a second hourly-rate overhead; it budgets separate project-level coordination and tooling work.
The 30% seller asking factor is a negotiation choice, not a market-observed IP discount.
Market, income and strategic proxies share the same cost anchor; they are correlated model scenarios, not three independent valuations.
No per-project hours are reverse-engineered from a published price and presented as independently estimated effort.
Missing whole-project work budgets and missing price-basis source heads are explicitly reported, not inferred from current README files.
All four model lenses share the same recreation anchor. Their weighted blend is an internal sensitivity, not independent triangulation.

Scoped implementation budgets add only the stated non-overlapping work to the retained scope component. Asking and negotiation references preserve the seller-selected asking/cost relationships with EUR 500 rounding. Unmerged candidate work is excluded unless expressly priced.
Sequential scoped increments reconcile through their successive anchors. Earlier budgets retain their historical totals; they are not each required to equal the final anchor.
methodology.futureRule: Only R→P and P→V maturity transitions receive a numeric conditional reference. V-stage assets receive NOT_ESTABLISHED unless new attributable market/income evidence supports a separate model. An independently owned asset without its own monetary inputs has no numeric sensitivity until those inputs are established.
methodology.futureCalculation: Recompute the published market, income, strategic and triangulated reference using the target-stage factors from economic-methodology.json while holding invariant inputs constant.
methodology.calculationPolicy: Recalculate the four cost-model outputs for each asset from the disclosed inputs. Apply Math.round to each non-negative whole-EUR scenario, then calculate and round the weighted blend from those rounded scenarios. Asking prices, negotiation bounds and recreation estimates are disclosed seller inputs, not independently validated market values. An unlisted sector or route retains the original neutral factor 1 and is explicitly identified in the calculation trace.
methodology.factorCalibration: All maturity, potential, marketability, commercialisation, rights reserve, sector and route factors are seller-selected scenario assumptions. Their numeric values are not independently calibrated success probabilities, transaction discounts or measured market observations.

reassessment.runtimeBoundary: Current local software checks and retained source-specific evidence are reviewed separately. reassessment.budgetCoverageBoundary: Coverage describes the arithmetic and stated scope of seller budgets, not external price validation or whole-product production acceptance.
reassessment.portfolioBoundary: Portfolio figures are sums of individual references. They do not establish a package price or account for shared replacement work, integration costs, dependencies or buyer-specific synergies.
reassessment.developmentRecognition: Implemented, bounded, non-overlapping work can receive an explicit incremental reproduction estimate. Renames, version numbers, elapsed days, pending proposals and additional test counts alone do not determine monetary value.
